LESSON: GUIDED WRITING GRAMMAR HANDWRITING PUNCTUATION SENTENCE STRUCTURE

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: FRENCH
Strand: Writing 3. 5 Guided writing Handwriting Punctuation Vocabulary Grammar Clarity B
Topic 3.6: Guided Writing Grammar Handwriting Punctuation Sentence structure

SECTION 1: WELCOME

• Today’s class: Guided Writing Grammar Handwriting Punctuation Sentence structure
• How we learn: Teach → Worked example → Try this
• Use point notes. Show working. Then take the quiz.
• Big question: Why is proper sequencing of information important while writing?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

1. write common words with correct orthography
2. appreciate the role of writing in interactive communication contexts
3. write common words with correct orthography
4. appreciate the role of writing in interactive communication contexts
5. spell in writing common words with correct orthography
6. construct simple sentences using correct structures
7. appreciate the role of writing in interactive communication contexts
8. spell in writing common words with correct orthography

SECTION 3: CLASS STUDY (TEACH → EXAMPLE → TRY)

▸ Guided Writing Grammar Handwriting Punctuation Sentence structure

• Listen to a model.
• Study the example.
• Then produce your own example.

▸ Guided Writing Grammar Handwriting Punctuation Sentence structure

Teach
• Focus skill: write common words with correct orthography.
• Use complete sentences.
• Speak clearly; write neatly.

Worked example
• Model sentence 1 about Guided Writing Grammar Handwriting Punctuation Sentence structure.
• Model sentence 2 using a Kenyan school example.
• Model dialogue: A: “…?”  B: “…”

Try this
• Write 5 original sentences on this skill.
• Say one 30-second oral example to a partner.


SECTION: QUICK EXAMPLES

• One clear model for Guided Writing Grammar Handwriting Punctuation Sentence structure
• One Kenyan school/home example

SECTION: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences.
2. Do one oral practice with a partner.
3. Correct spelling/punctuation.

SECTION: WORK TO DO

1. Revision sheet: meaning + 5 examples + 5 practice items.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why is proper sequencing of information important while writing?
2. How can you improve your handwriting?
3. Why is correct orthography important?
4. What makes your handwriting unique?

SECTION: REMEMBER

• Model first, then try.
• Use complete sentences.

• Next: complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Classroom study notes (Strategy 2)
